# Nalu

> Nalu (Hawaiian: the wave that reaches the shore) is a small typed language for setup, build, deploy and install scripts. A `.nalu` file compiles to Bash (Linux 4.3+, macOS 3.2) and PowerShell (Windows 5.1+), with no runtime on the target. This is the compact specification for language models; the full reference is docs/language.md and the standard library is docs/stdlib.md (or `nalu doc <name>`).

## Rules that cause the most mistakes (read first)

- Nalu is not Rust, Swift, Go or JavaScript. There is one way to do each thing, and the compiler names the right one when you use another.
- Interpolation is `{expr}` inside double quotes. `{{` and `}}` are literal braces. Fixed JSON: single quotes `'{"a": 1}'` (no interpolation, no escapes). Interpolation is the only way to turn a value into text.
- There is no `try` per line, `throws`, `?`, `null` or exceptions: EVERY operation that can fail, without `catch`, stops the script (or makes the enclosing function fail). Handle failures with `catch`.
- Logic is `||`, `&&` and `!`. There is no `or`, `and` or `not`.
- `let` is immutable; `var` is mutable. No `const`, no `++`/`--`.
- Functions: `fn name(a: int, b: str = "x") -> str { … }`. No `function`, `def` or `func`.
- Types like Go: `[]str`, `[]int`, `[][]str`, `map[str]int`, `map[str][]str`. A struct field can be another struct.
- Loops: `for x in xs`, `for i, x in xs`, `for k, v in m`, `for n in 0..10` (excludes 10), `0..=10` (includes it), `while cond { }`.
- `if` and `match` are expressions: `let r = if c { 1 } else { 2 }`. No ternary `?:`.
- `match x { … }` has one arm per line, tried in order: `"a" | "b" => …`, `200..=299 => …`, `n if n >= 500 => "error {n}"` (a name takes the value; `if` is a guard), `Service { port: 443 } => …` (struct pattern), `_ => …`. Enum cases are written without the type name inside `match`; a `match` on an enum must cover every case or end with `_`.
- snake_case names, PascalCase types. No `import`: the standard library is always available. To split a script, `use "lib.nalu"` at the start of a file brings in that file's `fn`, `struct`, `enum` and `test` declarations (still one script per target).
- `slice` works like JavaScript (negative counts from the end, `end` optional). `xs[i]` out of range FAILS (use `xs[i] catch default`).
- A command is a line that starts with `$ `. Unquoted words are literal (no globbing, no `$VAR`). `{x}` becomes ONE argument; a list `{xs}` alone becomes several. An unquoted ` catch ` ends the command.
- Maps: `m[k]` reads (can fail), `m[k] = v` writes. Empty checks: `s == ""`, `xs.len() == 0`. Nested values change in place: `grid[i][j] = v`, `svcs[0].port = 80`, `groups[k].push(x)`, `let x = rows[0].pop()`.
- Regex patterns are fixed text in single quotes: `regex.find(s, 'v\d+\.\d+')`. `find`/`find_all`/`groups`/`replace` need patterns with one way to match (`[^=]*=` instead of `.*=`).
- Paths: `.name`, `.stem`, `.ext`, `.parent` only look at the text and never fail; the disk is `fs.exists(p)`, `fs.is_dir(p)`, `fs.size(p)`, `fs.modified(p)`; join with `/`.
- An unused variable is a warning (W001); prefix it with `_` on purpose.

## Types

`str`, `int` (64-bit; `/` truncates), `bool`, `path` (`dirs.home() / "x"`), `duration` (`500ms`, `30s`, `1m30s`, `2h`, `7d`; does not mix with int: `d / 1s` gives an int), `secret` (never becomes text), `[]T` (items: scalars, structs or lists of scalars), `map[K]V` (`{ "a": 1 }`; values: scalars or lists of scalars), `struct` (fields can be structs or lists of structs), `enum`. No float.

## Failures

```nalu
fn load(p: path) -> str {
    return fs.read(p)  // if it fails, load fails (at the top level, the script stops)
}

let optional = fs.read("a.txt") catch ""          // default value
let port = env.get("PORT") catch fail "set PORT"  // fail with another message ({err} available)
$ git pull catch ignore                           // keep going (only without a value)
let n = "42".to_int() catch {
    log.warn("bad number: {err}")  // a block with `err`; the last line is the value
    0
}
try {
    $ git add .
    $ git commit -m "x"
} catch {
    exit(err.code)
}
print(load("b.txt"), optional, port, n)
fail "message", code: 3  // fail on purpose (code is optional)
```

`err.message`, `err.code`. These can fail: `$` commands, `$( )` captures, standard library functions marked as fallible, `.to_int()`, `.find()`, `.first()`, `.last()`, `.pop()`, `m[k]`, `xs[i]`, `Type.parse()`, `retry`, `parallel`, and any function of yours that contains one of these without `catch`. `nalu check --explain file.nalu` lists every line that can fail.

## Commands

```nalu
param image: str = "app"
param tag: str = "dev"
param token: secret

$ docker build -t {image}:{tag} .
let commit = $(git rev-parse --short HEAD)  // stdout without the trailing newline
token | $ docker login --password-stdin     // value through stdin
if $ git diff --quiet {
    print("clean at {commit}")
}
$ make all > build.log 2>&1
```

## A script

```nalu
/// shown in --help
param stage: Stage = Stage.dev
param version: str
param token: secret  // also read from NALU_TOKEN
param files: []str = []

enum Stage { dev, prod }

struct Service {
    name: str
    port: int

    fn url() -> str {
        return "http://localhost:{self.port}"
    }
}

let services = [Service { name: "api", port: 8080 }]
let tmp = fs.temp_dir()
defer fs.rm(tmp)  // runs at exit, even after a failure
token | $ docker login registry.example.com --password-stdin
parallel for s in services {
    $ docker push {s.name}:{version}
}
retry(10, every: 5s) {
    if http.status(services[0].url()) != 200 {
        fail "not up yet"
    }
}
if os == "windows" {
    print("{stage} {files.len()}")  // compile-time constant: "linux", "macos", "windows"
}
if dry_run {
    exit(0)  // every script takes --dry-run, --verbose and --help
}
```

Tests: `test "name" { … }` blocks with `assert cond` and `assert_fails(call())` on their own lines, in `x_test.nalu`, run with `nalu test`.

## Standard library (signatures; "!" = can fail)

- built-ins: `print(a, …)`, `exit(code = 0)`, `fail`, `fmt("{} {}", a, b)` (templates that come from data), `secret(s)`, `embed("file")`, `os`, `dry_run`, `args: []str`.
- env: `get(name)!`, `has(name)`, `set(name, value)`.
- fs: `exists(p)`, `is_dir(p)`, `is_file(p)`, `size(p)!`, `modified(p)!`, `read(p)!`, `write(p, text)!`, `append(p, text)!`, `rm(p)!`, `mkdir(p)!` (creates parents), `copy(from, to)!`, `move(from, to)!`, `ls(dir)!`, `walk(dir)!`, `glob(pattern)`, `temp_dir()!`, `temp_file()!`, `replace(p, from, to)!`, `chmod(p, mode)!` ("755", "+x"; no-op on Windows).
- path: `abs(p)`; properties `p.name`, `p.stem`, `p.ext`, `p.parent`; `a / "b"` joins.
- dirs: `home()`, `temp()`, `cwd()`, `config(app)`, `cache(app)`, `data(app)`.
- sys: `arch()` (x64, arm64), `hostname()`, `user()`, `is_admin()`, `is_ci()`, `cpus()`, `require_admin()!`, `cd(dir)!`.
- proc: `exists(cmd)`, `which(cmd)!`.
- time: `now()` (s), `now_ms()`, `since(t)`, `since_ms(t)`, `format(fmt = "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S", t = -1)`, `sleep(d)`, `hour(t = -1)`.
- log: `info`, `warn`, `error`, `debug` (stderr; debug only with --verbose).
- ui: `confirm(q)`, `ask(q, fallback = "")`, `password(q)!` → secret, `choose(q, options)!`.
- math: `min(a, b)`, `max(a, b)`, `abs(n)`.
- http: `get(url, timeout = 30s, headers: []str = [], bearer: secret = "")!`, `post(url, body, content_type = "application/json", timeout, headers, bearer)!`, `status(url, timeout, headers, bearer)!` → int, `download(url, to, headers, bearer)!`. Headers are "Name: value".
- json: `get(text, path)!` (text without quotes; numbers/lists/objects as JSON text; null fails), `get_list(text, path)!`, `keys(text, path)!`, `has(text, path)`, `quote(text)` (a JSON string with quotes). path: "a.b.0" or "a.b[0]"; "" is the root.
- hash: `sha256(text)`, `sha256_file(p)!`.
- regex (pattern = fixed text): `test(text, pattern)`, `find(text, pattern)!`, `find_all(text, pattern)`, `groups(text, pattern)!` → []str, `replace(text, pattern, new)` (`new` literal). Syntax: `. [a-z] [^,] \d \w \s * + ? {2,5} ( ) | ^ $`, `(?i)` at the start.
- encoding: `base64_encode(text)`, `base64_decode(text)!`.
- archive: `tar_create(file, dir)!`, `tar_extract(file, to)!`, `zip_extract(file, to)!`.
- str: `len()`, `trim()`, `trim_start()`, `trim_end()`, `upper()`, `lower()`, `contains(s)`, `starts_with(s)`, `ends_with(s)`, `strip_prefix(s)`, `strip_suffix(s)`, `index_of(s)` (-1), `slice(a, b)`, `split(sep)`, `lines()`, `replace(a, b)` (all), `replace_first(a, b)`, `repeat(n)`, `pad_left(n, c)`, `pad_right(n, c)`, `to_int()!`, `chars()`.
- lists: `len()`, `push(x)`, `pop()!`, `filter(f)`, `map(f)`, `any(f)`, `all(f)`, `find(f)!`, `contains(x)`, `index_of(x)`, `join(sep)`, `sum()`, `sort()`, `sort_by(f)`, `reverse()`, `slice(a, b)`, `unique()`, `first()!`, `last()!`. Lambdas: `x => x > 1` or `x => { … return v }`.
- maps: `m[k]!`, `m[k] = v`, `has(k)`, `remove(k)`, `keys()`, `values()`, `len()`.
- Planned (the compiler refuses it with E090): pkg.

## CLI

`nalu run x.nalu -- args`, `nalu build x.nalu [--target linux,macos,windows] [-o dist]`, `nalu check x.nalu [--json] [--explain]`, `nalu check --stdin x.nalu --json` (source on stdin), `nalu fmt [files|folders]` (`--check` only checks; `--stdin x.nalu` for editors), `nalu doc [name…]` (docs for `fs`, `fs.copy`, `str`, `str.split`, `catch`…; no name: the overview), `nalu emit x.nalu --target T`, `nalu test [folder]`, `nalu ide hover|complete|signature|definition|context x.nalu --at L:C [--stdin]` (editor queries, JSON). After writing or editing Nalu code, run `nalu fmt` and `nalu check`; when unsure about a function, `nalu doc`.

## Complete example

```nalu
/// folder to compress
param folder: path = "."
/// where to keep the backup
param dest: path = "~/backups"

fn compress(src: path, archive_file: path) -> int {
    if !fs.is_dir(src) {
        fail "{src} is not a folder"
    }
    archive.tar_create(archive_file, src)
    return fs.size(archive_file)
}

fs.mkdir(dest)
let archive_file = dest / "{folder.name}-{time.format("%Y%m%d")}.tar.gz"
let size = compress(folder, archive_file) catch {
    log.error("backup failed: {err}")
    exit(1)
}
fs.write(archive_file.parent / "{archive_file.name}.sha256", "{hash.sha256_file(archive_file)}  {archive_file.name}\n")
log.info("{archive_file} ({size / 1024} KB)")
```
